newsitem.title: UK: UK pro-Europeans warn of cost of EMU opt-out.
newsitem.headline: UK pro-Europeans warn of cost of EMU opt-out.

text.p: Pro-Europeans warned British companies on Tuesday that they would pay an economic price in higher interest rates if Britain opted out of the first wave of countries joining a single currency.

In a document being sent to banks, financial institutions and industry, the European Movement warned that financial markets could see a refusal to join as signalling a desire to pursue a less responsible monetary policy.

In addition, the document said, Britain would have no say in major policy decisions taken by the European Central Bank which would have a major impact on its economy, such as the choice of monetary instruments and the inflation target.

The document also attacked claims by opponents of economic and monetary union that it would lead to Britons helping to pay for other countries' pensions, lead to big fiscal transfers to poorer EU regions and bring higher unemployment.

"There is a real danger that precisely because some of their (critics') allegations are so fanciful, no one will bother to refute them," said Conservative MP Quentin Davies, vice-chairman of the European Movement.
"The effect of monetary union will be to impose a natural discipline on Government borrowing. That can only be a thoroughly good thing," Davies added.
"Some might, in theory, wish to preserve the right to ruin ourselves, but this is not a position likely to gain much support from the financial markets or the general public," he said.

Labour MP Giles Radice, the movement's chairman, said he wanted to stress the benefits the single currency would provide in terms of lower interest rates which would spur business investment and mean cheaper mortgages for home owners.
